question: Under standard precautions, when should a nurse wear gloves?

options.A: Whenever you give oral medications to older adults
options.B: Whenever there is a chance of touching blood or body fluids
options.C: During every single interaction with any patient
options.D: Only when caring for patients in isolation rooms

explanation: Standard precautions apply to everyone. If you expect contact with moist body substances, glove up!

question: Which of these is a main goal of doing passive range of motion?

options.A: Increasing active muscle strength
options.B: Lowering high blood pressure instantly
options.C: Keeping joint flexibility and movement
options.D: Treating underlying bone infections

explanation: Well done! Passive movements are specifically designed to keep joints flexible when a patient cannot move themselves.

question: If a needle has a lower gauge number, what does that tell you about its size?

options.A: The needle length is shorter
options.B: The needle width is larger
options.C: The syringe barrel is smaller
options.D: The needle tip is sharper

explanation: Needle gauges can be tricky! Just remember: the smaller the gauge number (like 20G), the thicker and wider the needle is. A higher number (like 25G) is much thinner.

question: Why must a nurse check the pulse and skin color below a fractured limb?

options.A: To check for signs of blood vessel or nerve damage
options.B: To calculate the exact date when the bone will heal
options.C: To prevent the development of a systemic bone infection
options.D: To determine how much calcium the patient's body needs

explanation: Swelling or displaced bone fragments can pinch nearby arteries and nerves, cutting off blood supply and sensation to the fingers or toes. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T13#GNS221_U3_T13_h3)

question: Which liver enzyme is known to be more specific to liver cell injury?

options.A: AST
options.B: Amylase
options.C: ALT
options.D: Lipase

explanation: Spot on! Alanine aminotransferase (ALT) is concentrated mostly inside liver cells, making it a reliable red flag when liver tissue is damaged.

question: Which of these is NOT a common system challenge in many healthcare settings?

options.A: Severe shortages of essential life-saving drugs
options.B: Excessive availability of well-trained nursing staff
options.C: Frequent interruptions in electrical power supply
options.D: Financial burdens caused by out-of-pocket payments

explanation: Spot on! Having too many well-trained staff is rare. Instead, staff shortages are a major challenge in resource-constrained systems.

question: How does a procedure called marsupialization stop a Bartholin cyst from coming back?

options.A: By surgically removing the entire gland and surrounding tissue
options.B: By sealing the gland shut so it stops producing any fluid
options.C: By stitching the edges of the cyst open to create a permanent little pouch
options.D: By packing the internal cavity tightly with sterile gauze

explanation: Marsupialization sounds fancy, but it just means sewing the walls of the cyst open so it turns into a tiny pouch. This stops fluid from getting trapped again!

question: What is a super important piece of discharge teaching for a patient on antibiotics for a bone infection?

options.A: Switch to topical creams once the IV line is removed
options.B: Stop taking the drugs the moment pain subsides
options.C: Double the dose if a fever returns for one evening
options.D: Finish the entire prescription even if symptoms disappear

explanation: Always remind patients to finish every single pill! Stopping early can let the stubborn bacteria bounce back stronger.

question: What should you do when a patient suddenly falls silent during an emotional discussion?

options.A: Changing the topic immediately to lighten the mood
options.B: Rushing to fill the silence with medical facts
options.C: Tolerating silence and allowing the patient time to gather thoughts
options.D: Leaving the room until the patient starts speaking again

explanation: Sitting quietly without rushing shows deep respect and gives vulnerable patients the space they need to process heavy emotions. Take a bow!

question: Why must you check a patient's kidney function before a contrast-enhanced CT scan?

options.A: Contrast dye can strain the kidneys and worsen poor function
options.B: Poor kidneys make patients allergic to all drugs instantly
options.C: Contrast dye causes the urinary bladder to shut down
options.D: Kidney problems stop the CT machine from taking clear pictures

explanation: Iodine contrast can be tough on the kidneys, so we always check renal function first to keep our patients safe.

question: How many months of cycle tracking are generally recommended before relying on the calendar method?

options.A: Only one single month
options.B: Six to twelve months
options.C: Five whole years
options.D: Exactly two weeks

explanation: Tracking past cycles for several months helps you find a reliable pattern of your shortest and longest cycles, which is needed for the math to work out!

question: A clinic notices a sudden drop in teenagers coming in for counseling. What is the best next step?

options.A: Blame the local school teachers for poor student attendance
options.B: Close the clinic permanently and transfer staff to another district
options.C: Increase user fees to attract a wealthier class of patients
options.D: Investigate possible barriers like staff attitude or operating times through youth feedback

explanation: A drop in numbers is a warning sign. Checking in with the youth helps you pinpoint the problem—whether it's bad staff attitude or inconvenient opening hours—so you can fix it!

question: What is a key instruction the nurse must give the patient before the procedure starts?

options.A: Take deep breaths continuously while the needle is in place
options.B: Remain as still as possible and avoid coughing during insertion
options.C: Stand up and walk around the room to help settle the fluid
options.D: Drink at least two liters of water right before the procedure

explanation: Sudden movements or coughs can cause the needle to scrape or puncture the delicate lung tissue. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T17#GNS221_U2_T17_h4)

question: Why do intestinal cells have to package dietary fats into structures called chylomicrons?

options.A: To convert fats directly into glucose
options.B: To neutralize stomach acid in the gut
options.C: To allow transport into lymphatic lacteals
options.D: To make the fat molecules taste sweet

explanation: Fats are too bulky to slip directly into blood vessels, so enterocytes package them into chylomicrons so they can travel safely through the lymphatic vessels.

question: For a couple under 35 years old, how long do they usually try to conceive through unprotected sex before doctors consider it infertility?

options.A: Twelve months or more
options.B: Three months or less
options.C: Six to nine months
options.D: At least two years

explanation: You've got this! Doctors look at a full 12 months of regular, unprotected sex as the standard timeline before testing for fertility issues. Keep up the great work!

question: Why do pregnant women have a significantly higher nutritional requirement for specific minerals like iron?

options.A: To support expanding blood volume and fetal growth
options.B: To completely prevent gestational diabetes mellitus
options.C: To replace electrolytes lost through morning sickness
options.D: To cure pre-existing chronic bone infections

explanation: Pregnancy causes a major increase in blood volume and requires extra nutrients to support the developing fetus and placenta. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T20#GNS214_U1_T20_h3)

question: What is the most important nursing check right after a patient has a liver biopsy?

options.A: Remove all intravenous access lines right away
options.B: Monitor vital signs and check the puncture site for bleeding
options.C: Feed the patient a large high-fiber meal immediately
options.D: Encourage the patient to walk briskly around the hospital ward

explanation: Since the liver has a huge blood supply, watching closely for bleeding and checking vital signs is top priority after this procedure.

question: Why do patients in the early stages of asphyxia often look restless and confused?

options.A: Their digestive system has shut down
options.B: The brain is not receiving enough oxygen
options.C: Their blood pressure is abnormally high
options.D: They are having an allergic skin reaction

explanation: The brain is very sensitive to oxygen levels. When it starts running low, the patient often gets anxious, confused, or restless before losing consciousness.

question: If someone accidentally swallows or breathes in a small object, why is it more likely to go down the right bronchus?

options.A: The left bronchus is blocked by the heart's position
options.B: The right bronchus is wider, shorter, and more vertical
options.C: The right lung has three lobes instead of two
options.D: Air flows at a much faster speed on the right side

explanation: Correct! The right main tube makes a much straighter, wider path down from the windpipe, making it an easier slipway for anything unwanted.

question: Why does passing urine normally help protect your body from infections?

options.A: It physically flushes out bacteria before they can stick to the tract
options.B: It coats the bladder wall with a thick protective mucous layer
options.C: It neutralizes the pH of the urine to stop bacterial growth
options.D: It increases the core body temperature to kill pathogens

explanation: Think of regular urination like a natural tap flush! It sweeps invading germs out of the system before they can settle down and cause trouble.

question: Your patient has a GI bleed. You notice their heart rate is rising and their blood pressure is falling. What does this most likely mean?

options.A: Normal recovery from bleeding
options.B: Developing hypovolemic shock
options.C: A sudden spike in blood sugar
options.D: Effective fluid volume overload

explanation: Brilliant deduction! When blood volume drops, the heart beats faster to try and compensate, but eventually blood pressure drops as shock sets in. You're thinking like a real nurse!

question: Why is the real-world failure rate for natural methods usually higher than the textbook 'perfect use' rate?

options.A: Manufacturing defects occur in calendar charts
options.B: Human error and inconsistent tracking happen in daily life
options.C: Body temperature sensors expire after one month
options.D: Government policies restrict natural birth control methods

explanation: A method might look foolproof on paper, but real life gets busy! Missing a day of charting or miscalculating a window easily leads to human error.

question: What is the normal range for intracranial pressure (ICP) in an adult?

options.A: 80 to 120 mmHg
options.B: 5 to 15 mmHg
options.C: 120 to 140 mmHg
options.D: 30 to 50 mmHg

explanation: Normal ICP stays between 5 and 15 mmHg. This keeps blood flowing nicely to the delicate brain tissues without crushing them.

question: A client with rheumatoid arthritis wakes up with severe joint stiffness that lasts for nearly two hours. What does this tell you as a nurse?

options.A: It represents normal muscle fatigue from daily exercise
options.B: It indicates active and ongoing systemic inflammation
options.C: It suggests the client is experiencing a sudden bone fracture
options.D: It points to a localized soft tissue injury from a fall

explanation: Morning stiffness that drags on for an hour or more is a major red flag for active inflammation inside the joints. Great nursing assessment catches this early!

question: Why is accurate and prompt charting of IV care crucial for nursing practice?

options.A: It is the only way hospital administrators calculate nurse salaries
options.B: It stops patients from asking nurses repetitive questions about fluids
options.C: It provides a clear legal record of care and ensures safe continuity among staff
options.D: It replaces the need for verbal shift handovers between nursing teams

explanation: Good documentation proves professional standards were met and helps the next shift monitor the site safely. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T4#GNS122_U1_T4_h10)

question: What postnatal sign shows that the uterus is slow to shrink back down to its normal pre-pregnancy size?

options.A: Increased breast engorgement
options.B: Elevated maternal temperature
options.C: Uterine subinvolution
options.D: Rapid lochia cessation

explanation: Subinvolution is just a medical term for when the womb takes way too long to go back to its normal size and tone, often leading to longer-than-normal bleeding.

question: What should you do first if you spot an unexplained, non-healing sore on a patient's tongue?

options.A: Scrape the surface firmly to see if it bleeds like thrush
options.B: Prescribe an antibacterial mouthwash for two weeks
options.C: Document its exact size, shape, and refer for medical evaluation
options.D: Advise the patient to stop using commercial toothpaste

explanation: Always record clear details of the lesion and send the patient for a proper medical review to rule out anything serious.

question: Which part of the brain acts like an alarm clock to keep us physically awake?

options.A: The peripheral nervous system
options.B: The spinal cord reflex arcs
options.C: The Ascending Reticular Activating System
options.D: The cerebellum and basal ganglia

explanation: Think of the ARAS as the brain's main power switch or alarm clock, sending constant wake-up signals from the brainstem to keep the cerebral cortex alert.

question: What is the most reliable daily indicator of fluid balance changes in a hospitalized child with nephritis?

options.A: Morning body temperature
options.B: Skin color assessment
options.C: Abdominal girth measurement
options.D: Daily body weight

explanation: Daily weighing is the single most sensitive and accurate way to track fluid retention or loss in patients with kidney problems. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T4#GNS213_U4_T4_h7)

question: A patient comes in feeling constantly exhausted, has gained weight, hates cold weather, and has dry, coarse hair. What condition do these signs point to?

options.A: Hypothyroidism
options.B: Hyperthyroidism
options.C: Cushing's syndrome
options.D: Addison's disease

explanation: You've got this! These are classic signs of a sluggish metabolism caused by not having enough thyroid hormones in the body.

question: A patient recovering from bowel surgery starts eating normal food again, but complains of sharp cramps and nausea. What should you do first?

options.A: Give a strong laxative to clear them out
options.B: Pause the food advancement and inform the doctor
options.C: Switch them immediately to total IV nutrition
options.D: Encourage them to finish the meal to build strength

explanation: Cramps and nausea are your tummy's way of saying 'not yet!' Slowing down and resting the gut prevents bigger problems like blockages.

question: What is the main reason for putting an artificial airway in an unconscious patient?

options.A: To prevent the tongue from sliding back during feeding
options.B: To allow the administration of oral liquid medications
options.C: To protect against aspiration and maintain clear breathing
options.D: To measure core body temperature continuously

explanation: You're doing great! Unconscious patients can't protect their airway or swallow properly, so a tube keeps air flowing and stops saliva or vomit from entering the lungs.

question: What is the primary nursing priority immediately after a patient returns from a cardiac catheterization via the femoral artery?

options.A: Removing the pressure dressing to inspect the exact puncture wound
options.B: Encouraging the patient to get out of bed and walk around the room
options.C: Checking the insertion site for bleeding and monitoring distal pulses
options.D: Administering a large dose of oral potassium supplements immediately

explanation: Arterial access carries a high risk of bleeding and loss of blood flow to the leg, so nurses must frequently check the puncture site and the pulse in the foot. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T13#GNS213_U1_T13_h2)

question: Why is assessment in palliative care an ongoing cycle rather than a one-time thing?

options.A: Hospital policies require daily paperwork updates from the nursing staff
options.B: Patient conditions and symptoms shift as the illness progresses
options.C: Insurance companies demand new symptom scores before paying bills
options.D: Doctors change their minds about medications every few hours

explanation: Because serious illnesses change rapidly, as nurses we need to keep checking in so we can catch new discomforts early.

question: Why must a single unit of blood be completely infused within a maximum of four hours?

options.A: To prevent bacterial multiplication in the blood product at room temperature
options.B: To allow the nurse to finish the shift before the bag is empty
options.C: To ensure the patient does not become bored during the procedure
options.D: To prevent the blood from freezing inside the intravenous tubing

explanation: Blood is kept cold for a reason! Once it sits at warm room temperature for too long, bacteria love to multiply in it, which can put the patient at risk for severe infection.

question: Why does the WHO stress having a steady supply of injection equipment?

options.A: Having extra supplies makes nurses finish their shifts much faster
options.B: Patients refuse treatment if clinics do not show them brand new boxes
options.C: Shortages often force workers to reuse single-use devices out of desperation
options.D: Government regulations require clinics to store at least ten years of stock

explanation: When clinics run out of disposables, it puts immense pressure on nurses. Reliable supplies keep everyone safe from risky workarounds.

question: When is it completely unsafe to give a patient medication by mouth?

options.A: When the drug is manufactured as a small tablet
options.B: When the patient is unconscious or unable to swallow
options.C: When the medication is inexpensive to produce
options.D: When the patient has a mild headache

explanation: Great nursing instinct here! If a patient cannot swallow or is unconscious, giving oral meds puts them at severe risk of choking and getting fluid into their lungs.

question: Which of these steps must you always do first before disinfecting or sterilizing equipment?

options.A: Packaging
options.B: Cleaning
options.C: Disinfection
options.D: Sterilization

explanation: Always wash off blood, dirt, and tissue first! If dirt is left on the tool, it shields the germs from the disinfecting or sterilizing agents.

question: Why are commercial pastries and doughnuts a bad idea for a patient on a low-fat diet?

options.A: They lack sufficient calories to maintain basic metabolic energy
options.B: They cause immediate kidney failure by blocking renal tubules
options.C: They contain large amounts of hidden shortening, butter, and oils
options.D: They neutralize all digestive enzymes in the small intestine

explanation: You nailed it! Baked goods often hide heavy amounts of fats and oils used during preparation.

question: A patient catches malaria after being bitten by an infected mosquito. How would you classify this transmission?

options.A: Direct contact transmission
options.B: Airborne transmission
options.C: Vector-borne transmission
options.D: Vehicle-borne transmission

explanation: Mosquitoes, ticks, and other living creatures that carry germs to us are called vectors. That makes this a classic vector-borne disease!

question: A nurse meets a shy 15-year-old girl from a low-income home who expresses fear of getting pregnant. What is the most appropriate nursing intervention?

options.A: Inform her parents right away without discussing it with the teenager first
options.B: Focus the discussion entirely on unrelated physical symptoms like headaches
options.C: Provide non-judgmental counseling, education on contraception, and connect her with youth-friendly resources
options.D: Tell the teenager to stop speaking with boys immediately and send her home

explanation: Empowering teens with practical knowledge and supportive resources is the most effective nursing approach to prevent adverse outcomes. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T9#GNS312_U3_T9_h9)

question: What is the main job of the skin's natural lipids (fats) found between skin cells?

options.A: They fight off local germs like your body's immune system
options.B: They make skin pigment to block the sun's rays
options.C: They give the deeper skin layer its stretch and bounce
options.D: They act like mortar to lock in moisture and keep germs out

explanation: Think of skin cells like bricks and these lipids like the mortar between them. This oily seal keeps your hydration locked in and prevents harmful invaders from entering.

question: What size of IV catheter is preferred for fast fluid replacement in a severe trauma patient?

options.A: Midline catheter with dual lumens
options.B: Large-bore catheter like 16 or 18 gauge
options.C: Small-bore catheter like 24 gauge
options.D: Peripherally inserted central catheter

explanation: Think of an IV line like a pipe: a wider pipe (16 or 18 gauge) lets fluids and blood flow in much faster during an emergency.

question: A patient is scheduled for an MRI. What is the most critical safety check for you to do first?

options.A: Ensuring the patient drinks two liters of water
options.B: Testing the patient's blood pressure and pulse rate
options.C: Checking if the patient has eaten any food that morning
options.D: Screening for implanted metal devices or pacemakers

explanation: MRI magnets are extremely powerful! Any metal inside the body—like pacemakers or metal clips—can shift, heat up, or malfunction, putting the patient in serious danger.

question: When is the standard comprehensive postnatal check usually scheduled after the initial hospital stay?

options.A: At one year
options.B: At six months
options.C: At six weeks
options.D: At two weeks

explanation: The six-week postnatal visit is the big milestone where we check that both the mother's body and mind have fully recovered from pregnancy and birth. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h9)

question: Why are nurses considered the heartbeat of safe hospital waste management?

options.A: They design and build medical incinerators
options.B: They purchase all hospital waste disposal bags
options.C: They generate and supervise the sorting of the majority of clinical waste
options.D: They write national environmental protection laws

explanation: Because nurses carry out most bedside procedures, your daily choices make or break how well hospital waste gets sorted!

question: Why is looking at community data just as important for a nurse as giving bedside care?

options.A: Clinical procedures are secondary to statistical data collection
options.B: Patients refuse care unless statistics are explained first
options.C: Data helps identify community service gaps and allocate resources
options.D: Hospitals require nurses to publish annual demographic research

explanation: Bedside care is vital, but looking at the big picture data helps us find villages or groups who are missing out on care so we can send help where it's needed most!

question: When did Nigeria introduce its first official National Drug Policy to fix chaotic drug distribution?
explanation: Nigeria rolled out its very first formal National Drug Policy back in 1990 to clean up unregulated drug imports and fight fake medicines.

question: In a burn wound, what is the central area called where the maximum tissue damage happens?

options.A: Zone of hyperemia
options.B: Zone of inflammation
options.C: Zone of stasis
options.D: Zone of coagulation

explanation: Think of the zone of coagulation as ground zero—it's closest to the heat, so the cells are completely destroyed and can't recover. You've got this!

question: When is a newborn baby usually most awake and ready to try breastfeeding for the very first time?

options.A: Between twelve and twenty-four hours after delivery
options.B: Right after receiving their routine Hepatitis B immunization
options.C: During the first period of reactivity immediately after birth
options.D: During deep sleep cycles following nursery admission

explanation: Right after birth during that first hour of life, babies are super alert and eager to feed. It's the golden window for bonding!

question: Which global region currently has the highest number of maternal deaths?

options.A: North America
options.B: Southeast Asia
options.C: Sub-Saharan Africa
options.D: Western Europe

explanation: As future Nigerian nurses, knowing our local context is key. Sub-Saharan Africa bears the heaviest load of maternal mortality, making our work so important.

question: Why is emotional and psychological support so important in high-risk pregnancy care?

options.A: Patients on bed rest have nothing else to do during the day
options.B: Mental health counseling replaces the need for medical check-ups
options.C: Chronic stress and anxiety can negatively affect both maternal and fetal well-being
options.D: It guarantees the mother will have a natural vaginal delivery

explanation: Mind and body are connected! High stress releases hormones that can impact the pregnancy, so a comforting word from you as a nurse goes a long way.

question: Which of these is an environmental hazard that can cause falls at home?

options.A: Well-lit hallways
options.B: Secured handrails in bathrooms
options.C: Cluttered walkways and loose rugs
options.D: Low-heeled supportive footwear

explanation: Loose rugs and messy pathways are classic trip hazards. Clearing them is a simple and life-saving way to keep older adults safe from falls.

question: What major service makes a comprehensive emergency obstetric care center different from a basic one?

options.A: Episiotomy repair
options.B: Manual placenta removal
options.C: Cesarean section
options.D: Perineal tear suturing

explanation: Spot on! Comprehensive centers can handle major surgeries like Cesarean sections and blood transfusions when basic care isn't enough.

question: What does it mean if a patient has a congenital absence of a fallopian tube?

options.A: The tube was blocked by scar tissue from endometriosis
options.B: The tube failed to form during embryonic development
options.C: The tube was surgically removed due to infection
options.D: The tube was destroyed by a ruptured ectopic pregnancy

explanation: Spot on! 'Congenital' simply means present from birth, meaning the tube never developed in the first place.

question: Which layer of the heart wall does the actual hard work of pumping blood?

options.A: Pericardium
options.B: Endocardium
options.C: Myocardium
options.D: Epicardium

explanation: The myocardium is made of strong muscle tissue. Every time your heart beats, it's the myocardium doing the heavy lifting to push blood out!

question: What should the nurse do immediately if a patient complains of severe burning under a poultice?

options.A: Wait another hour to see if it stops
options.B: Tie the bandage tighter to stop the burning
options.C: Tell the patient to endure the pain
options.D: Remove the poultice and wash the skin

explanation: Severe burning means the application is too hot or irritating, requiring immediate removal to prevent skin injury. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T10#GNS221_U3_T10_h7)

question: Which blood-borne infection has the highest statistical risk of transmission after a single accidental needle-stick?

options.A: Hepatitis C virus
options.B: Human Immunodeficiency Virus
options.C: Hepatitis B virus
options.D: Cytomegalovirus

explanation: Hepatitis B is remarkably hardy and infectious. That is why getting your Hep B vaccine and safety training early in nursing school is so important!

question: What is the correct temperature range for storing most routine vaccines in a clinic fridge?

options.C: +2°C to +8°C

explanation: You got it! Keeping vaccines between +2°C and +8°C keeps them fresh and effective without freezing them by accident.

question: Which tool do doctors commonly use to look inside the uterus and remove small fibroids?

options.A: Bronchoscope
options.B: Otoscope
options.C: Colonoscope
options.D: Hysteroscope

explanation: A hysteroscope is gently passed through the cervix to check the inside of the uterus and fix structural issues directly.

question: Which of these is a great example of an open-ended question you can ask a patient?

options.A: Asking 'How are you coping with your illness today?'
options.B: Nodding silently without asking any questions at all
options.C: Asking 'Did you take your morning blood pressure pill?'
options.D: Telling the patient 'You need to stop worrying so much.'

explanation: Well done! Open-ended questions can't be answered with a simple 'yes' or 'no', which encourages your patient to open up and share more.

question: What is the main medicine used to treat a confirmed bacterial lower respiratory infection?

options.A: Antibiotics
options.B: Antihistamines
options.C: Antifungals
options.D: Antivirals

explanation: Since it's a bacterial infection, antibiotics are needed to target and stop those specific germs from multiplying.

question: What is the main goal of gender-responsive communication in healthcare?

options.A: To provide care free from gender bias and assumptions
options.B: To eliminate the use of medical terminology with patients
options.C: To ensure all patients receive the exact same treatment
options.D: To focus solely on biological differences between sexes

explanation: Spot on! When we communicate without gender bias, our patients feel safe, respected, and truly understood.

question: What happens to a reflex if the sensory neuron gets damaged or cut?

options.A: Only the integration center will process the signal.
options.B: The brain will take over the reflex function.
options.C: The reflex response will fail to occur.
options.D: The effector will react continuously without stopping.

explanation: Think of a reflex arc like a relay race. If one runner (the sensory neuron) drops out, the message never reaches the finish line and the reflex doesn't happen.

question: Why is maintaining infection control standards especially challenging in under-resourced hospitals?

options.A: A lack of interest from senior medical consultants
options.B: Excessive amounts of personal protective equipment
options.C: Patients refusing to take prescribed medications
options.D: Unpredictable water supply and shortages of basic safety supplies

explanation: Frequent utility failures and lack of continuous basic commodities make standard cleaning and barrier methods much harder to sustain daily. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h2)

question: Why would a doctor order a skin KOH (potassium hydroxide) test?

options.A: To dissolve skin keratin and check for fungal elements under a microscope
options.B: To test for immediate severe allergic reactions to local anesthetic drugs
options.C: To measure the exact electrical resistance across a thickened skin plaque
options.D: To destroy abnormal surface cells using controlled freezing temperatures

explanation: Spot on! The KOH solution melts away the tough skin keratin so any sneaky fungus or yeast hiding underneath becomes easy to see.

question: Why should you and your patient set nutrition goals together instead of you just giving orders?

options.A: Patients are more likely to follow goals they helped create
options.B: Patients always know more about clinical nutrition than nurses
options.C: Hospital policies legally prohibit nurses from choosing diet plans
options.D: Collaborative goals eliminate the need for future follow-up visits

explanation: Exactly! When patients have a say in their plan, they feel a sense of ownership and are way more likely to stick with it.

question: A patient with heart failure shows sudden weight gain and severe shortness of breath. What does this mean?

options.A: They are severely dehydrated
options.B: Their heart muscle is successfully healing
options.C: They gained sudden muscle mass
options.D: Worsening fluid overload and congestion in the lungs

explanation: That sudden weight gain isn't fat or muscle—it's trapped water! When heart failure worsens, fluid pools up in the body and lungs, making breathing really tough.

question: What is the term for that exciting moment when a mother first feels the baby fluttering inside her womb?

options.A: Quickening
options.B: Balottement
options.C: Lightening
options.D: Engagement

explanation: Quickening is the mother feeling the baby move for the first time! It's a classic presumptive sign because only she can feel it.

question: You touch a hot pot in the clinical kitchen and instantly pull your hand back. Which fibers carried the signal from your CNS out to your hand muscles?

options.A: Sensory fibers
options.B: Efferent fibers
options.C: Receptor fibers
options.D: Afferent fibers

explanation: E-fferent exits the brain with instructions (think 'E' for exit). Quick reflexes keep future nurses safe! [learn more](GNS211_U3_T2#GNS211_U3_T2_h4)

question: Why do nurses look at a patient's skin as a mirror of their inner health?

options.A: Skin changes often appear before systemic disease symptoms show
options.B: The skin controls all chemical reactions in the human body
options.C: External skin temperature dictates core metabolic rate completely
options.D: Internal organs directly push pigment through the dermal layers

explanation: The skin often gives us early warning signs. Changes in color, texture, or rashes can show up before other internal sickness symptoms even start!

question: A patient comes to the clinic with severe belly pain and rectal bleeding after using a local herbal enema. What is the biggest nursing concern here?

options.A: Severe allergic rhinitis and upper airway swelling
options.B: Sudden complete obstruction of the upper esophagus
options.C: Trauma to the rectal mucosa and systemic toxicity
options.D: Immediate development of peripheral neuropathy

explanation: Harsh local enemas can easily tear the delicate lining of the rectum and quickly push strong, unmeasured chemicals straight into the bloodstream. Ouch! Patient safety is key here.

question: During the final delivery of the baby's body, which part usually comes out first?

options.A: The posterior hip
options.B: The umbilical cord
options.C: The anterior shoulder
options.D: The lower extremities

explanation: Spot on! The front shoulder slips out from under the pubic bone first, and then the back shoulder follows.

question: What is the most common reason a patient with sickle cell anaemia is rushed to the emergency ward?

options.A: Diabetic ketoacidosis
options.B: Vaso-occlusive pain crisis
options.C: Hypertensive emergency
options.D: Acute kidney failure

explanation: Spot on. When sickled cells block blood flow, tissues get starved of oxygen, triggering intense pain crises that bring patients straight to the hospital.

question: Which two common bacteria are most often responsible for causing salpingitis?

options.A: Treponema pallidum and Trichomonas vaginalis
options.B: Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus
options.C: Neisseria gonorrhoeae and Chlamydia trachomatis
options.D: Streptococcus pneumoniae and Klebsiella pneumoniae

explanation: Chlamydia and gonorrhea are the sexually transmitted bacteria behind the vast majority of acute salpingitis cases. Great to keep in mind for clinical practice!

question: A patient with active pulmonary tuberculosis is admitted to the ward. Which intervention is most crucial to interrupt the airborne transmission of this disease?

options.A: Providing the patient with disposable plastic utensils
options.B: Placing the patient in a negative pressure isolation room
options.C: Washing all hospital floors with ordinary tap water daily
options.D: Encouraging family members to wear clean cloth gloves

explanation: Airborne pathogens require specialized ventilation, such as negative pressure rooms, to prevent them from spreading through the air to other areas. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T95#GNS214_U1_T95_h3)

question: What does the term 'bereavement' mean in nursing care?

options.A: The physical pain felt in the chest after a loss
options.B: The deliberate suppression of sad emotions
options.C: The objective state of having lost someone through death
options.D: The outward religious rituals performed at a funeral

explanation: You've got this! Bereavement is simply the factual reality that someone you care about has passed away. It is the starting point where grief and mourning begin.

question: A patient scheduled for surgery takes daily aspirin for joint pain. What is your main concern as their nurse?

options.A: Aspirin causes a dangerous spike in white blood cell counts
options.B: Aspirin inhibits platelet function and can cause excessive bleeding
options.C: Aspirin turns the patient's blood bright green in the tubing
options.D: Aspirin completely stops the kidneys from producing urine

explanation: Aspirin stops platelets from sticking together properly. Before surgery, this puts the patient at high risk for heavy bleeding.

question: Which global body defines nursing as autonomous and collaborative care for people of all ages in all settings?

options.A: West African Health Organization
options.B: International Council of Nurses
options.C: Red Cross International
options.D: World Medical Association

explanation: Spot on! The International Council of Nurses sets the global standard definition that highlights both our independent and teamwork roles in healthcare. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h3)

question: A patient asks which part of the ABCD strategy guarantees 100% protection from sexually transmitted HIV. What is the best response?

options.A: Abstinence
options.B: Using condoms
options.C: Taking vitamins
options.D: Being faithful

explanation: Spot on! Complete abstinence is the only strategy that offers absolute protection against sexually transmitted HIV.

question: What is the primary definition of haemorrhage?

options.A: A sudden increase in red blood cell production
options.B: The movement of fluid from tissue into capillaries
options.C: The localized clotting of blood inside a vein
options.D: The escape of blood from the vascular system

explanation: Haemorrhage simply means bleeding, which is the loss of blood from damaged blood vessels, either inside or outside the body. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T4#GNS123_U3_T4_h1)

question: What is the main purpose of an under-water seal drainage system?

options.A: To restore negative pressure in the pleural space
options.B: To measure the exact daily urine output of a patient
options.C: To pump sterile water directly into the lung tissue
options.D: To deliver high-flow oxygen straight into the chest cavity

explanation: The primary goal of chest tube drainage is to evacuate air or fluid, thereby re-establishing the normal negative pressure needed for lung expansion. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T15#GNS213_U2_T15_h1)

question: Why are daily reviews of invasive lines and breathing tubes an important part of complication prevention?

options.A: Hospital insurance policies require equipment to be changed daily.
options.B: It gives the nursing staff less paperwork to complete at shift change.
options.C: Removing them as soon as they are no longer needed lowers infection risks.
options.D: Patients prefer to have new lines poked into them every morning.

explanation: Every day a tube or line stays inside the body gives bacteria more time to enter and cause a severe infection. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T4#GNS321_U2_T4_h5)

question: According to Kübler-Ross, which stage of grief happens when a person tries to make a deal with God or fate to change what is happening?

options.A: Acceptance
options.B: Anger
options.C: Denial
options.D: Bargaining

explanation: In the bargaining stage, people try to negotiate or make promises to try and postpone or reverse an inevitable loss. You've got this!

question: Which physical finding is the classic hallmark of a patient with a vesicovaginal fistula?

options.A: Total absence of urine output for over 48 hours
options.B: Inability to walk due to paralysis of both legs
options.C: Severe lower abdominal swelling and tenderness
options.D: Continuous leakage of urine from the vaginal vault

explanation: You got it! Constant wetness is the tell-tale sign because urine flows straight into the vagina instead of collecting in the bladder. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T12#GNS216_U5_T12_h3)

question: You need to give medications to two patients in your ward. What should you do with your equipment?

options.A: Rinse the syringe with hot water between patients
options.B: Change only the needle and keep the same syringe barrel
options.C: Use the same syringe if the drug is prescribed for both
options.D: Use a fresh, sterile syringe and needle for each patient

explanation: Syringes and needles are strictly single-use. Never share them between patients—ever!

question: Which sign tells you that a child's breathing problem is getting worse and turning into respiratory failure?

options.A: Slow, irregular breathing and cyanosis
options.B: An increase in spontaneous talking
options.C: Loud, powerful crying and high energy
options.D: Rapid, deep breathing with normal skin color

explanation: At first, a struggling child breathes super fast. But once their muscles get too tired, they slow down, breathe irregularly, and turn blue (cyanosis). That's a true emergency!

question: Which of these makes a topical medication much more likely to absorb into the bloodstream and cause toxicity?

options.A: Washing the skin thoroughly with mild soap and water
options.B: Applying the cream over large areas of broken skin
options.C: Rotating the application site with every dose
options.D: Using a clean tongue depressor to spread the ointment

explanation: When skin is broken, its natural protective barrier is gone, letting too much medicine flood into the bloodstream. Good clinical awareness!

question: Why should nurses avoid vague phrases like 'skin looks infected' in professional charting?

options.A: It slows down the discharge planning process for the medical team
options.B: It prevents the patient from reading their own medical chart history
options.C: It automatically violates hospital legal policies regarding privacy protection
options.D: It lacks the specific, objective details required to evaluate treatment efficacy

explanation: Vague words don't give enough detail. Saying '1cm red area with pus' tells the whole team much more than just 'infected'.

question: What is a major danger of the social stigma surrounding abortion in healthcare?

options.A: Clients may delay seeking life-saving medical care out of fear
options.B: Hospital pharmacies automatically run out of emergency drugs
options.C: Infection rates drop because patients use home remedies first
options.D: Doctors are legally required to discharge patients within hours

explanation: Fear of harsh words or mistreatment often makes women wait too long to come to the hospital, which sadly makes their physical complications much worse.

question: When you are checking if a patient is fully 'oriented,' what three key things do you ask about?

options.A: Sight, hearing, and touch
options.B: Height, weight, and age
options.C: Pulse, temperature, and blood pressure
options.D: Person, place, and time

explanation: Checking person, place, and time is the classic, quick way to test if a patient's brain is alert and aware of their surroundings.

question: What type of clothing is best for someone working outdoors in areas with lots of stinging insects?

options.A: Brightly colored floral shirts that blend with nature
options.B: Shorts and sleeveless tops to stay cool in the heat
options.C: Light-colored, long-sleeved clothing that fits smoothly
options.D: Dark wool garments to absorb sweat effectively

explanation: You got it! Smooth, light-covered, long clothes protect your skin and help you avoid attracting insects that love dark colors and floral patterns.

question: What is a key part of holistic nursing care for survivors of harmful traditional practices?

options.A: Focusing strictly on surgical interventions while ignoring emotional needs
options.B: Prescribing strong sedative medications to keep the patient quiet
options.C: Encouraging the patient to cut off all ties with her local community
options.D: Combining physical wound treatment with psychological counseling and social support

explanation: Exactly! Holistic care means healing the whole person—mind, body, and emotions—not just fixing a physical wound.

question: You are about to use a sterile pack, but you are not completely sure if the seal was broken. What should you do?

options.A: Assume it is contaminated and discard or re-sterilize it
options.B: Check if the expiration date on the package is still valid
options.C: Use it only for non-invasive bedside procedures
options.D: Wipe it down with alcohol and proceed with the task

explanation: When in doubt, throw it out! In sterile technique, any uncertainty means the item is no longer safe to use. Better safe than sorry!

question: Why are bedside nurses considered the frontline defenders in clinical risk management?

options.A: They decide which doctors get suspended for errors.
options.B: They handle all legal lawsuits filed by patients.
options.C: They observe daily workflows and spot hazards firsthand.
options.D: They write the official hospital policies and budget plans.

explanation: Bedside nurses work directly with patients every day, placing them in the best position to notice subtle workflow issues and safety risks. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T9#GNS312_U5_T9_h1)

question: What is your best first step if a portable monitor starts showing crazy, unreadable numbers?

options.A: Throw the equipment into the nearest biohazard bin
options.B: Inspect cable connections and sensor placement
options.C: Take the device apart with a screwdriver to check internal wires
options.D: Ignore the error message until the shift ends

explanation: Usually, erratic data just means a loose cable or a slipped sensor. Always check the physical setup first!

question: What is a crucial first step when a palliative patient suddenly develops acute delirium?

options.A: Double the dose of all routine daily medications
options.B: Instantly tie the patient's hands to the bed rails for safety
options.C: Turn off all lights and leave the patient completely alone
options.D: Search for and treat reversible underlying triggers like infection or pain

explanation: Delirium is often a symptom of an underlying physical issue like a UTI, constipation, or hypoxia that needs correction. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T15#GNS321_U4_T15_h6)

question: Why do patients on standard chemotherapy often experience hair loss and mouth sores?

options.A: The chemical makeup of the drugs directly dries out the outer layers of human skin.
options.B: The radiation energy absorbed by the bloodstream weakens oral and scalp tissues.
options.C: Patients naturally stop eating enough fresh fruits and vegetables due to nausea.
options.D: The medications attack all rapidly dividing cells, including healthy normal cells like hair follicles and mucosal linings.

explanation: Exactly! Chemotherapy targets fast-growing cells. Sadly, it can't tell the difference between cancer cells and our healthy fast-growing cells, like hair and gut linings.

question: What is a major reason why patients struggle to take antiretroviral therapy over a long period?

options.A: Lack of available water in the community
options.B: Doctors changing the prescription daily
options.C: Daily pill fatigue and complex routines
options.D: Automatic expiration of medicine bottles

explanation: The requirement to take medications every single day for the rest of one's life often leads to exhaustion and missed doses. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T7#GNS216_U6_T7_h3)

question: What is the primary goal of a physiotherapist working with an older adult?

options.A: Reviewing daily prescription drug charts for errors
options.B: Assisting with feeding during meal times
options.C: Providing emotional counseling for depression
options.D: Improving mobility, strength, and balance to prevent falls

explanation: Physiotherapists use guided exercises and movement training to help older adults stay steady, strong, and safe from falls.

question: What is the primary purpose of using a genogram during a family health assessment?

options.A: To track daily movement outside the neighborhood
options.B: To calculate the monthly food budget
options.C: To measure home square footage and ventilation
options.D: To map out inherited medical conditions and family history across generations

explanation: Think of a genogram as a medical family tree. It helps you quickly spot patterns of chronic illnesses like hypertension or diabetes.

question: A patient looks pale and feels dizzy halfway through a large fluid drain. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Push the drainage catheter further into the skin
options.B: Inform the doctor and monitor vital signs closely
options.C: Leave the room to document the procedure chart
options.D: Encourage the patient to drink a glass of water

explanation: Dizziness and paleness mean the blood pressure might be dropping. Alerting the team and checking vitals keeps the patient safe.

question: Which part of the small intestine connects directly to the stomach?

options.A: Jejunum
options.B: Cecum
options.C: Duodenum
options.D: Ileum

explanation: The duodenum is that C-shaped first stop where food leaves the stomach and meets up with juices from the liver and pancreas.

question: Why do patients with these disorders sometimes show sudden changes like anger or unfriendliness (apathy)?

options.A: Temporary side effects from routine physical therapy sessions
options.B: Inadequate daily fluid intake causing mild dehydration
options.C: Normal psychological adjustment to aging processes
options.D: Damage to frontal lobe structures controlling mood and behavior

explanation: The frontal lobe is like our brain's emotional dashboard. When it gets damaged, managing moods becomes really tough for the patient.

question: Why are nurses in a great position to act as health educators?

options.A: They receive no medical training and speak like ordinary people
options.B: They are the only healthcare professionals legally allowed to teach
options.C: They spend continuous time at the bedside interacting with patients
options.D: They control the hospital budget for educational supplies

explanation: Spot on! Because nurses are always around, we can break teaching down into small, easy steps over time.

question: In simple terms, what does endocrine 'hyposecretion' mean?

options.A: Hormones are destroyed in the bloodstream
options.B: A gland produces too little of a hormone
options.C: A gland produces too much of a hormone
options.D: Target organs completely reject hormones

explanation: You've got this! 'Hypo-' always means under or low. So hyposecretion just means the gland isn't making enough hormone.

question: A patient remains on strict bed rest for several days after surgery. Why does this lack of movement increase their risk of blood pooling in the legs?

options.A: It causes arteries to dilate and flood the lower extremities with fluid
options.B: It stops the skeletal muscle pump from assisting venous return
options.C: It destroys the one-way valves inside the deep capillary networks
options.D: It immediately thickens the blood cells inside the small arterioles

explanation: Skeletal muscle contraction is necessary to physically compress veins and push low-pressure blood upward, so inactivity promotes pooling. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T5#GNS111_U2_T5_h4)

question: A conscious patient's random blood sugar is 52 mg/dL and they feel shaky. What should you do right away?

options.A: Give 15 grams of fast-acting oral carbohydrates
options.B: Send the patient for an emergency CT scan of the head
options.C: Inject long-acting insulin into the deltoid muscle
options.D: Wait patiently for two hours and test the blood again

explanation: Since the patient is awake and able to swallow, give them quick-acting sugar (like glucose tablets or juice) to bring their blood sugar back up safely.

question: What is a major safety rule nurses must follow when a patient is in the lithotomy position?

options.A: Turning the patient every thirty minutes without fail
options.B: Padding the stirrups to protect nerves and blood vessels
options.C: Keeping the head of the bed elevated to 90 degrees
options.D: Removing all pillows from beneath the patient's head

explanation: Bare metal stirrups can pinch nerves and block blood flow in the legs. Always make sure those stirrups are well-padded!

question: Who is considered a skilled birth attendant?

options.A: A family member who has given birth multiple times
options.B: Any volunteer working at a local health post
options.C: A trained health professional such as a nurse or midwife
options.D: An experienced traditional birth healer in the community

explanation: Spot on! A skilled birth attendant is a certified professional, like a nurse or midwife, trained to manage normal births and handle emergencies.

question: What happens when a patient internalizes societal HIV stigma?

options.A: They experience intense self-blame and shame
options.B: They immediately disclose their status to everyone
options.C: Their CD4 cell count automatically rises
options.D: They stop experiencing any physical symptoms

explanation: Internalized stigma causes patients to direct society's harsh judgments inward, leading to deep shame and self-blame. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T7#GNS216_U6_T7_h4)

question: What is the go-to medication for stopping and preventing seizures in severe preeclampsia?

options.A: Diazepam tablets
options.B: Magnesium sulfate
options.C: Calcium gluconate
options.D: Hydralazine injection

explanation: You're doing great! Magnesium sulfate is the gold standard for managing eclamptic seizures and keeping mothers safe. A true midwifery essential!

question: Which route of administration is best for treating a sudden, life-threatening allergic reaction?

options.A: Inhaled powder
options.B: Oral tablet
options.C: Topical cream
options.D: Intravenous

explanation: Spot on! The intravenous (IV) route pushes the medication straight into the bloodstream for instant action during emergencies.

question: Why do we have to be extra careful when disposing of cytotoxic (chemotherapy) drugs?

options.A: Expired tablets turn into sweet-tasting candy that attracts children
options.B: These drugs instantly catch fire when exposed to ordinary air
options.C: Cytotoxic drugs are designed to destroy cells and can damage healthy tissue and genetic material
options.D: Chemotherapy drugs make the local soil extremely fertile for crops

explanation: Spot on! These medications are specially made to kill fast-growing cells, meaning they can harm healthy human tissue and our environment if carelessly thrown out.

question: In the popular SBAR communication tool used by healthcare workers, what does the letter 'B' stand for?

options.A: Behavior
options.B: Breath
options.C: Bedside
options.D: Background

explanation: SBAR is a handy way to report patient info! 'B' stands for Background, giving the listener the essential history leading up to the current moment.

question: What is the medical word for the changing shape of a baby's skull caused by pressure during labour?

options.A: Moulding
options.B: Caput succedaneum
options.C: Flexion
options.D: Ossification

explanation: Moulding is simply the shifting and overlapping of the skull bones that temporarily alters the baby's head shape to fit the pelvis. It's totally normal!

question: Why do doctors urgently order a CT scan of the head for a patient who suddenly becomes unconscious?

options.A: To quickly spot bleeding, blood clots, or structural brain damage
options.B: To measure the exact electrical activity firing across the cortex
options.C: To check for bacterial growth within the cerebrospinal fluid
options.D: To determine if the patient has ingested specific toxic drugs

explanation: Brilliant! A CT scan gives a fast, clear picture to see if there is dangerous bleeding or a blood clot that needs immediate attention.

question: What does the top number in a blood pressure reading represent?

options.A: Systolic pressure when the heart rests
options.B: Systolic pressure when the heart beats
options.C: Diastolic pressure when the heart rests
options.D: Diastolic pressure when the heart beats

explanation: The top number is the systolic pressure, which measures the force in the arteries when the heart contracts or beats. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T16#GNS324_U4_T16_h1)

question: Which topic is typically evaluated during a psychosocial and lifestyle assessment?

options.A: Tobacco, alcohol, and substance use habits
options.B: Results of microscopic blood cultures
options.C: Detailed cellular structure of body tissues
options.D: Exact surgical technique used in an operation

explanation: Lifestyle assessments cover daily habits, including substance use, diet, exercise, and stress levels. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T2#GNS123_U2_T2_h7)

question: During a home visit, a patient with severe anxiety mentions thoughts of ending their life. What is the nurse's priority action?

options.A: Tell the patient to snap out of it and focus on positive thoughts
options.B: Wait until the next scheduled clinic appointment in two weeks
options.C: Advise the patient to exercise vigorously until exhausted
options.D: Assess the immediate suicide risk and ensure a safe environment

explanation: You nailed it. Safety always comes first. When a patient talks about self-harm, assessing immediate risk is the most crucial step.

question: Which low-cost test is commonly used in Nigerian primary health clinics to check for early cervical cell changes?

options.A: Endoscopic retrograde cholangiography
options.B: Visual Inspection with Acetic Acid
options.C: Positron emission tomography scans
options.D: Magnetic resonance imaging scans

explanation: Correct! VIA (Visual Inspection with Acetic Acid) is quick, affordable, and works wonderfully in everyday primary care clinics where high-tech scanners aren't available.

question: Why does the midpiece of a spermatozoon contain a large concentration of mitochondria?

options.A: To protect the genetic material from chemical damage
options.B: To manufacture extra testosterone during transit
options.C: To help the sperm attach securely to the egg wall
options.D: To produce enough energy for the tail to swim

explanation: Mitochondria act as cellular powerhouses, generating the ATP energy necessary for the flagellum to propel the sperm. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T7#GNS216_U2_T7_h6)

question: Why is getting enough rest emphasized as a way to prevent breast infections in nursing mothers?

options.A: Rest stops the baby from crying during the night
options.B: Lying down automatically cures blocked milk ducts
options.C: Sleeping prevents milk from ever being produced in the alveoli
options.D: Fatigue lowers the immune response, making the body more prone to infection

explanation: When a new mother is exhausted, her immune system struggles to fight off invading bacteria. Rest is vital care!

question: In palliative care, who is considered the 'unit of care' alongside the patient?

options.A: The hospital administration board
options.B: The insurance case manager
options.C: The family and informal caregivers
options.D: Only the primary attending physician

explanation: Palliative care recognizes that serious illness impacts everyone close to the patient, making family support an essential component of the care plan. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T13#GNS321_U4_T13_h5)

question: How do blood vessel (vascular) diseases lead to erectile dysfunction?

options.A: By causing excessive testosterone production in the testes
options.B: By blocking the normal production of seminal fluid
options.C: By destroying the nerves of the cremasteric muscle
options.D: By impairing adequate blood flow into the cavernous tissues

explanation: You got it! An erection needs good, healthy blood flow to fill the tissues. If vascular disease gets in the way, that flow is restricted.

question: When exercising the lower limbs, where should you place your hands to support the leg?

options.A: Under the knee and under the heel
options.B: Right on the kneecap and toes
options.C: Around the middle of the thigh bone
options.D: Firmly on the client's hip bones

explanation: Spot on! Supporting the leg at the knee and heel keeps the patient comfortable and gives you steady control.

question: Which combination of symptoms is a major red flag for a postpartum uterine infection?

options.A: Mild swelling in both ankles
options.B: Foul-smelling lochia and fever
options.C: Gradual lightening of lochia color
options.D: Increased appetite and energy

explanation: Spot on! Fever combined with lower tummy pain and bad-smelling lochia are classic signs that the uterus might be infected and needs medical attention.

question: Why must anticholinergic drugs be avoided in patients with narrow-angle glaucoma?

options.A: They dilate blood vessels inside the retina
options.B: They cause permanent blindness instantly
options.C: They dissolve the cornea over time
options.D: They can dangerously increase eye pressure

explanation: Correct! Blocking acetylcholine makes the pupil widen, trapping fluid inside the eye and causing a dangerous spike in pressure.

question: What is a major benefit of peer support groups for people with physical disabilities?

options.A: Enforcing strict government compliance with building codes
options.B: Providing a safe space to share coping strategies and reduce loneliness
options.C: Offering specialized surgical treatments for mobility restoration
options.D: Replacing the need for family interaction entirely

explanation: Well done! Peer groups are wonderful because meeting others facing similar challenges helps kill loneliness and shares great life tips.

question: What did ancient Egyptians mix into vaginal pastes to block sperm?

options.A: Purified petroleum jelly
options.B: Boiled palm oil extracts
options.C: Liquid synthetic hormones
options.D: Crocodile dung and honey

explanation: History is wild! Ancient Egyptian records show they used sticky mixes like honey and crocodile dung as early barriers to block sperm.

question: A patient starting HIV treatment is worried about forgetting their daily pills. What is a helpful nursing action?

options.A: Tell the patient to stop taking the pills if they feel well
options.B: Help the patient set up phone reminders and a pill organizer
options.C: Suggest that missing a few doses per month has no real effect
options.D: Advise the patient to take a double dose whenever one is missed

explanation: Simple tools like daily pill boxes and phone alarms are fantastic practical ways to help patients stick to their routine.

question: What is a common sign of 'silent aspiration' in someone with swallowing difficulties?

options.A: Red flushing of the cheeks and forehead
options.B: A wet, gurgling voice sound after swallowing
options.C: Excessive sweating on the palms of the hands
options.D: A sudden spike in blood pressure

explanation: That wet or gurgling sound is a classic red flag! It often means a little bit of food or liquid slipped past the vocal cords without triggering a cough.

question: Which finding around a gastrostomy stoma site requires immediate reporting to the healthcare provider?

options.A: A small amount of dried crusting around the tubing
options.B: Purulent drainage and spreading skin redness
options.C: Mild pinkness that disappears after gentle cleaning
options.D: Normal skin tone matching the rest of the abdomen

explanation: Pus and spreading redness are classic signs of a localized infection that may require antibiotic treatment or adjusted wound care. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T4#GNS212_U1_T4_h5)

question: Why do doctors give steroid injections to a mum whose baby is coming much too early due to severe preeclampsia?

options.A: To drop the mother's blood pressure instantly
options.B: To stop her labour contractions completely
options.C: To help the baby's lungs mature quickly
options.D: To stop the mother from having seizures

explanation: Preterm babies often struggle to breathe on their own. Steroids give their tiny lungs a helpful boost of maturity before they arrive!

question: Why is it recommended to gently press on the tragus after instilling ear drops?

options.A: It prevents earwax from hardening further
options.B: It warms up the liquid drops inside the canal
options.C: It helps move the medication down into the ear canal
options.D: It seals the ear completely to block out loud noises

explanation: Pumping the tragus gently creates a mild suction effect that helps the drops travel down the canal toward the eardrum. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T10#GNS122_U1_T10_h6)

question: What is the safest site for giving an intramuscular injection to an adult?

options.A: Dorsogluteal
options.B: Vastus lateralis
options.C: Deltoid
options.D: Ventrogluteal

explanation: You got it! The ventrogluteal site is clear of major nerves and blood vessels, making it the safest choice for adult IM injections.

question: In a rehabilitation team, who is considered the most important person sitting at the very center of care?

options.A: The lead physical therapist
options.B: The charge nurse
options.C: The patient and family
options.D: The attending physician

explanation: You've got this! Rehabilitation is all about the patient and their loved ones. They are active partners in recovery, not just bystanders watching the care happen.

question: A patient has a urinary catheter in the ICU. What is the most important step a nurse can take to prevent a catheter-related infection?

options.A: Changing the urinary drainage bag every twelve hours
options.B: Removing the catheter as soon as it is clinically unnecessary
options.C: Irrigating the catheter with sterile saline twice per shift
options.D: Applying antibiotic ointment to the urethral meatus daily

explanation: The longer a catheter stays in, the higher the infection risk. Taking it out the moment it's no longer needed is the best defense!

question: What does it mean when a hormone comes from an 'ectopic' source?

options.A: An infection inside the anterior pituitary gland
options.B: An autoimmune reaction destroying thyroid receptors
options.C: A tumor outside the normal endocrine system that makes hormones
options.D: A complete failure of the hypothalamus to signal organs

explanation: Ectopic just means 'out of place'! It happens when abnormal tissues or cancer cells outside the usual glands start making hormones on their own. You're building great clinical knowledge. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T7#GNS211_U1_T7_h2)

question: What is the final long-term outcome if chronic glomerulonephritis keeps progressing without control?

options.A: End-stage renal disease requiring dialysis or transplant
options.B: Permanent stabilization without medical treatment
options.C: Transition of the disease into chronic liver failure
options.D: Complete recovery of normal kidney structure

explanation: When nephrons are gradually destroyed over time, the kidneys eventually stop working entirely, meaning the patient will need dialysis or a kidney transplant to survive.

question: How do Instrumental Activities of Daily Living (IADLs) differ from basic ADLs?

options.A: IADLs involve more complex tasks needed to live independently in the community.
options.B: IADLs require no thinking, just muscle strength.
options.C: IADLs are learned before basic self-care.
options.D: IADLs only focus on physical hygiene.

explanation: Think of basic ADLs as surviving day-to-day, while IADLs are the next level up—like cooking, shopping, and handling money—that help someone live on their own.

question: A patient scheduled for a CT scan with contrast says they have a severe allergy to shellfish. What should you do first?

options.A: Proceed with the scan because shellfish has no link to dye
options.B: Encourage the patient to drink extra water for one hour
options.C: Administer an oral dose of calcium supplements right away
options.D: Notify the healthcare provider immediately before the test

explanation: Shellfish allergies often overlap with iodine-based contrast allergies. Always alert the doctor right away so they can order premedication or choose a safer option.

question: How can you keep hands clean in a clinic when the running water supply stops?

options.A: Use set-up handwashing stations like Veronica buckets and alcohol rubs
options.B: Wipe hands clean with ordinary office paper towels
options.C: Wear the same pair of examination gloves all day long
options.D: Skip handwashing until municipal water lines are fully restored

explanation: Brilliant! Improvised running-water setups like Veronica buckets and alcohol-based rubs keep patient care safe even when the taps go dry.

question: Why is it encouraged to use local resources during resource mobilisation?

options.A: It guarantees free medical supplies from the World Bank
options.B: It stops the community from working together
options.C: It builds self-reliance and reduces project dependency
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for any planning

explanation: Using local resources ensures the community can sustain the project even if external donors pull out. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T5#GNS124_U4_T5_h6)

question: When does an infection officially count as a healthcare-associated infection?

options.A: Before the patient ever enters the clinic
options.B: Immediately following any minor injection
options.C: At least 48 hours after hospital admission
options.D: Within the first two hours of arrival

explanation: The 48-hour window helps differentiate infections the patient brought in with them from those caught while inside the facility. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h1)

question: How is segmentation different from peristalsis in the gut?

options.A: Segmentation occurs only in the stomach while peristalsis is in the colon.
options.B: Segmentation mixes food back and forth rather than moving it forward.
options.C: Segmentation is controlled by the brain while peristalsis is automatic.
options.D: Segmentation stops all digestion while peristalsis speeds it up.

explanation: You're doing great! While peristalsis pushes food forward, segmentation uses ring-like squeezes to thoroughly blend food back and forth with digestive juices.

question: What is the best way for a patient to clear the remaining radioactive tracer out of their body after a PET scan?

options.A: Taking a hot sauna bath to sweat out the toxins
options.B: Taking strong oral diuretics prescribed by the doctor
options.C: Eating high-fiber foods to speed up bowel movements
options.D: Drinking plenty of fluids and urinating frequently

explanation: Spot on! Fluids and frequent bathroom trips help flush the remaining radiopharmaceutical safely out through the kidneys.

question: What is a major benefit of primary nursing for patients?

options.A: Increased feelings of safety and better communication with a consistent nurse
options.B: Shorter waiting times in the hospital cafeteria
options.C: Elimination of all physical pain within twenty-four hours of admission
options.D: Guaranteed zero hospital bills upon discharge

explanation: Patients love seeing a familiar, caring face every day! It builds trust and cuts down the anxiety of hospital stays.

question: What type of care usually triggers automatic DRF exemptions during an emergency?

options.A: Long-term physical therapy
options.B: Annual medical fitness checkups
options.C: Emergency trauma resuscitation
options.D: Routine elective cosmetic surgery

explanation: When every second counts, emergency trauma care gets fast-tracked so lifesaving supplies are never delayed by paperwork.

question: What is a direct financial barrier to emergency obstetric care in poor communities?

options.A: Mandatory taxes on all pregnant women
options.B: Free distribution of essential obstetric medications
options.C: High transportation costs to reach the nearest health facility
options.D: Excessive availability of free community health centers

explanation: Lack of funds for transport often delays getting to the hospital during an obstetric emergency, worsening outcomes. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T6#GNS216_U1_T6_h2)

question: What is the best approach for managing pain in an infant who has just been circumcised?

options.A: Applying ice packs directly to the bare surgical wound for hours
options.B: Administering strong opioid medications every two hours around the clock
options.C: Keeping the infant awake so they do not feel the post-surgical pain
options.D: Using sweet oral sucrose solution alongside prescribed mild pain relievers

explanation: Sweet sucrose drops combined with safe, mild pain meds (like paracetamol) provide great comfort and pain relief for babies.

question: You are giving bed bath care to an unconscious patient with a head injury. Which nursing action is most important?

options.A: Massaging the back vigorously to improve general circulation
options.B: Washing the face with cold water to stimulate consciousness
options.C: Removing the cervical collar to wash the neck thoroughly
options.D: Preventing sudden neck twisting and keeping the head aligned

explanation: Well done! Keeping the head and neck straight and neutral stops the neck veins from getting squeezed, which prevents sudden, dangerous spikes in brain pressure.

question: Which of these traits tells us that a material is hazardous waste?

options.A: Biodegradable
options.B: Odorless
options.C: Flammable
options.D: Transparent

explanation: That's right! Materials that are flammable, corrosive, toxic, or reactive are flagged as hazardous and heavily regulated.

question: Why are strict professional boundaries so important in home health care?

options.A: Patients living at home rarely build emotional connections
options.B: Home health agencies forbid nurses from talking to family members
options.C: The domestic setting makes personal and professional lines easy to blur
options.D: Nurses are legally considered family members while inside the house

explanation: Spot on! When you're sharing tea and chatting in a living room, it's easy to forget you're working. Keeping healthy boundaries keeps both you and the patient safe.

question: Which specific brain cells are mainly destroyed in Parkinson's disease?

options.A: Cholinergic neurons in the peripheral nerves
options.B: Upper motor neurons in the cerebral cortex
options.C: Sensory neurons in the dorsal root ganglia
options.D: Dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra

explanation: Parkinson's specifically targets the cells that make dopamine in a brain area called the substantia nigra, affecting movement.

question: Why do nurses monitor urine output closely after a patient suffers severe bleeding?

options.A: To calculate the exact dietary protein intake required
options.B: To measure the effectiveness of routine infant feeding schedules
options.C: To evaluate renal perfusion and detect early kidney injury
options.D: To determine when the patient can be discharged home

explanation: When blood loss causes shock, the kidneys can suffer. Watching urine output helps us catch early signs of kidney trouble!

question: How does constraint-induced movement therapy help a client with weakness on one side of their body?

options.A: It builds bulk muscle strength in the weak arm through heavy weightlifting.
options.B: It forces the brain to use the weak side by restricting the strong side.
options.C: It permanently immobilizes the strong side to prevent accidental injury.
options.D: It eliminates pain in the joints by keeping the limbs completely still.

explanation: By gently resting or blocking the good arm, we trick and encourage the brain to wake up and practice using the weaker side, boosting neuroplasticity!

question: Why is training community stakeholders so important for health programs?

options.A: It generates financial profit for local hospitals
options.B: It allows them to prescribe pharmaceutical drugs independently
options.C: It turns them into active advocates who champion the cause
options.D: It replaces the need for community health extension workers

explanation: Training empowers leaders with knowledge so they can guide their people and sustain the health program locally. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T5#GNS124_U4_T5_h4)

question: Which specific bone cells are responsible for breaking down or resorbing bone tissue?

options.A: Osteons
options.B: Osteoblasts
options.C: Osteocytes
options.D: Osteoclasts

explanation: Remember: Osteoclasts 'c'rve or 'c'ut bone down! They break down old bone tissue to help with remodeling and keep blood calcium levels balanced.

question: What is the main way condoms stop pregnancy from happening?

options.A: By thickening cervical mucus permanently
options.B: By stopping ovulation in the ovaries
options.C: By trapping semen to keep sperm out of the uterus
options.D: By killing sperm cells inside the testes

explanation: Exactly right! Condoms act as a physical shield that catches semen so the sperm cannot swim up into the reproductive tract.

question: What is the main purpose of looking at clinical signs in tummy (gastrointestinal) problems?

options.A: To calculate the total hospital bill for the patient
options.B: To replace all lab tests and scans completely
options.C: To guess the exact day the patient will leave the hospital
options.D: To give us clues about how well the gut is working and looking

explanation: Signs and symptoms act like windows into the digestive tract, helping nurses and doctors figure out what is going wrong inside.

question: What is a common psychological consequence experienced by individuals with faecal incontinence?

options.A: Aggressive behavior toward healthcare staff
options.B: A sudden increase in overall self-confidence
options.C: Social isolation and fear of public accidents
options.D: Obsession with high-fiber diets

explanation: Fear of unexpected leakage and embarrassing odors often drives patients to withdraw from social activities and isolate themselves. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T8#GNS212_U1_T8_h8)

question: When assessing a skin boil or abscess, which physical sign tells you it is soft, filled with liquid, and ready for drainage?

options.A: Local pallor
options.B: Cool skin temperature
options.C: Fluctuation
options.D: Complete skin numbness

explanation: Fluctuation is just the clinical term for when the center feels bouncy or squishy under your fingers—that tells you liquid pus has gathered inside and it's ready to be let out!

question: Which body systems are most often targeted by poisons because they need constant energy and oxygen?

options.A: Skeletal and muscular systems
options.B: Central nervous and cardiovascular systems
options.C: Integumentary and lymphatic systems
options.D: Exocrine and endocrine systems

explanation: The brain and the heart work nonstop, making them very sensitive to any poison that disrupts their oxygen or metabolism.
